paragraph: For the complementation comparison, fix an input x and require finite branching and halting on every computation branch. The contrapositive of König's lemma (logic 2.10) makes the unfolded computation tree finite: an infinite finitely branching tree would have an infinite branch. Induction on this finite tree then gives the De Morgan duality: swap existential and universal nodes and interchange accepting and rejecting leaves, and each node's Boolean value is negated. In particular an all-universal decider complements the corresponding all-existential decider with swapped halting labels. A looping branch blocks this finite-tree argument; the least-fixed-point convention does not make looping reject in one machine and accept in its dual. Inputwise finiteness alone supplies no polynomial running-time bound.
beforeIdea: The computation tree is evaluated like a game tree: an existential node is an OR over its children, a universal node an AND, and halting leaves are the constants accept/reject (this is the NTM of toc-7.6 with the "some branch" rule applied only at $\exists$ states). The accepting computation is therefore not a path but a **subtree**: one child at each $\exists$ node and all children at each $\forall$ node. With all states existential the subtree is a single path (a certificate, NP); with all universal there is no choice and the machine accepts when every branch does (coNP); alternating the two kinds gives $\Sigma_k$ and $\Pi_k$ by running $k$ blocks of existential/universal states (3.5) — and, as 3.9 and 3.10 show, unbounded alternation reaches PSPACE and P.
